title: CNC Drilling Machine Hydraulic Requirements
scope_statement: Validated scope: generic hydraulic component classes, functional valve behavior, and direct port-to-port connectivity only. Pump/cylinder/reservoir sizing, pressure and flow ratings, line selection, filtration, cooling, prime mover selection, simulation and fabrication approval are explicitly deferred to the later sizing and engineering phases.
design_narrative: Repaired pressure-compensated open-circuit hydraulic topology with separate clamp and drill directional control. Tank supplies a pressure-compensated variable pump; pump pressure branches directly to the relief valve, the clamp DCV, and the forward sequence valve inlet. The clamp cylinder is controlled through a float-centre 4/3 ClampDCV and an actuator-port dual pilot-operated check valve. ClampDCV neutral vents both valve-side work lines to tank so the load lock can reseat for clamp hold. ForwardSequenceValve.X is piloted from the retained actuator-side clamp cap pressure at ClampLoadLock.A2, so drill-feed supply is enabled only after clamp pressure/completion is present while the clamp DCV can remain neutral. Drill feed extension supplies the cap chamber and meters rod-end exhaust through the selected one-way flow control. Drill return uses the free reverse direction of that flow control. The reverse sequence valve remains in the clamp rod/release work path: ClampDCV.B feeds ReverseSequenceValve.P, ReverseSequenceValve.A feeds ClampLoadLock.B1, and ReverseSequenceValve.X is piloted from the drill retract supply line at DrillFeedDCV.B so clamp release is unavailable until drill-retract pressure has risen. All valve returns and sequence drains return directly to Tank.R; repeated endpoints represent branches without tee or manifold components.

motion_control_decisions.justification: The actuator is confirmed horizontal and the load is resistive; numeric speed alone is treated as a sizing target, not a throttling topology requirement.
The clamp must retain position/force while another operation occurs; a static load-retention strategy is required. The load is horizontal/resistive, so dynamic counterbalance is not indicated.
Horizontal resistive return with no specified controlled speed or load-retention requirement during the retracting release motion.
The drill-feed motion is confirmed horizontal and works against a resistive drilling load; numeric feed speed alone is captured as a sizing target, not as a mandated flow-control topology.
Horizontal resistive retract with no specified controlled return speed, load holding, or overrunning condition.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: Open-circuit power, relief, and return manifold
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: Tank.S supplies Pump.S. Pump.P branches directly to ReliefValve.P, ClampDCV.P, and ForwardSequenceValve.P. ReliefValve.T, ClampDCV.T, DrillFeedDCV.T, ForwardSequenceValve.T, and ReverseSequenceValve.T return directly to Tank.R. The pressure-compensated pump supports standby delivery reduction while ClampDCV float neutral vents the clamp work lines.
ReliefValve.P is connected directly to Pump.P and ReliefValve.T returns directly to Tank.R. Relief setting is deferred to sizing/commissioning for the approximately 8 bar maximum system pressure.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: Clamp cylinder with float-centre directional control, dual pilot-check load lock, and reverse sequence valve in the clamp release work path
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: ClampDCV.A feeds ClampLoadLock.A1/A2 and ClampCylinder.Cap for clamp extension. ClampCylinder.Rod connects through ClampLoadLock.B2/B1 to ReverseSequenceValve.A; the sequence valve's integral A-to-P reverse check carries clamp-extend return to ClampDCV.B/T. Clamp release/retract pressure from ClampDCV.B must pass through ReverseSequenceValve.P-to-A before reaching ClampLoadLock.B1, so direct Pump.P supply to ClampDCV.P does not bypass the reverse interlock. ClampDCV neutral vents A1 and the B-side valve line to Tank.R so the dual pilot-operated check reseats and holds the clamp during drilling.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: Forward externally piloted pressure sequence plus drill rod-end meter-out feed and reverse-order interlock pilot
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: ForwardSequenceValve.P is supplied from Pump.P and its X pilot senses retained clamp cap pressure at ClampLoadLock.A2. Once clamp pressure/completion is proven, ForwardSequenceValve opens and supplies DrillFeedDCV.P. DrillFeedDCV extend supplies DrillFeedCylinder.Cap and exhausts DrillFeedCylinder.Rod through DrillFeedMeterOut in the metered A-to-B direction before returning through DrillFeedDCV.B/T to Tank.R. DrillFeedDCV retract supplies the rod chamber through the one-way flow control free B-to-A path and returns cap oil through DrillFeedDCV.A/T. DrillFeedDCV.B also pilots ReverseSequenceValve.X to prove drill retract pressure before clamp release.

design_decisions.decision: Use the pressure-compensated pump and separate clamp/drill directional valves, with ReverseSequenceValve in the clamp release work path.
design_decisions.rationale: Pump.P must supply ClampDCV.P for clamp advance, but clamp release is hydraulically interlocked by gating the ClampDCV.B-to-ClampLoadLock.B1 rod/release work path. Inserting ReverseSequenceValve there blocks release flow until drill retract pressure opens P-to-A, while the sequence valve's integral A-to-P reverse check preserves rod-side return during clamp extension.

design_decisions.decision: Pilot ForwardSequenceValve from ClampLoadLock.A2 instead of from the cylinder body port in the netlist.
design_decisions.rationale: ForwardSequenceValve.X must see the retained actuator-side clamp cap pressure while ClampDCV is neutral and venting the valve-side work lines. Using ClampLoadLock.A2 as the pilot source represents the locked, actuator-side clamping-pressure node directly and records the required closed-to-open state change from clamp hold to drill feed.

design_decisions.decision: Pilot ReverseSequenceValve from DrillFeedDCV.B, the drill retract supply work line.
design_decisions.rationale: The reverse interlock must have a demonstrable pressure source when DrillFeedDCV is in retract. DrillFeedDCV.B is the active rod-side retract supply node; the reverse sequence setting is commissioned so it opens only on the pressure rise associated with drill retraction completion at the end stop.

design_decisions.decision: Pair the clamp dual pilot-operated check with ClampDCV float-centre neutral.
design_decisions.rationale: The float-centre state vents ClampDCV.A and ClampDCV.B to tank, which drains ClampLoadLock.A1/B1 pilot pressure and allows the actuator-port checks to reseat for a provable no-drift clamp hold. Holding no longer depends on maintaining extend pressure during drilling.

design_decisions.decision: Install exactly one one-way flow control in the drill rod-end exhaust path.
design_decisions.rationale: The selected drill-feed phase requires non-compensated adjustable meter-out control during extension. The controlled path is DrillFeedCylinder.Rod to DrillFeedMeterOut.A, through the metered A-to-B path, then to DrillFeedDCV.B/T/Tank.R. Drill return uses the same component's free B-to-A reverse path, so no duplicate check valve is added.

design_decisions.decision: Do not add a clamp flow-control valve.
design_decisions.rationale: Clamp advance/retract speed is a sizing_only motion-control decision; numeric speed/force/travel targets are deferred to pump, cylinder, and valve sizing rather than requiring throttling topology.

assumptions: Feed completion and command to reverse are supplied by the machine control, not by added hydraulic topology.
Sequence valve pressure settings are deferred to sizing/commissioning, including the clamp-to-drill transition setting and reverse clamp-release setting.
The selected dual pilot-operated check represents the clamp actuator-port load-lock assembly at catalog granularity.
ForwardSequenceValve.X senses retained actuator-side clamp cap pressure at ClampLoadLock.A2 so ClampDCV can be neutral during clamp hold.
ReverseSequenceValve.X senses drill retract supply pressure at DrillFeedDCV.B; the reverse sequence setting is adjusted so the valve opens only when drill retraction is complete and pressure rises.
The drill actuator is treated as mechanically complete at its retracted end stop during clamp_release_retract.
open_issues: Sizing phase must verify cylinder areas, pump flow and valve settings for the approximate 8 bar pressure limit, clamp force, drill force and speeds.
Feed completion and command to reverse are assumed to be supplied by the CNC/machine control, not by added hydraulic topology.

Detailed netlist/phase review must confirm that ForwardSequenceValve.X senses actuator-side clamp pressure and ReverseSequenceValve.X senses drill-retract completion pressure without drain backpressure interference.
Sequence-valve settings, hysteresis, and reset behavior should be reviewed with the pressure-compensated pump and the drill rod meter-out path.

Because the reverse sequence valve is inserted in the clamp release work path, sizing/commissioning must verify that its integral A-to-P reverse check has adequate capacity for clamp-extend rod-side return flow.
Phase 'clamp_release_retract' selects ForwardSequenceValve.open without pressure at X.
Phase 'drill_feed_extend' selects ForwardSequenceValve.open without pressure at X.
Phase 'drill_return_retract' selects ForwardSequenceValve.open without pressure at X.
Phase transition 'clamp_extend_to_workpiece' -> 'clamp_hold_during_drilling' does not change a sequence_valve in the required way.

ForwardSequenceValve is commanded/open in the drill_feed_extend, drill_return_retract, and clamp_release_retract phase configurations, but the directed phase paths do not prove pressure at its X pilot port. The narrative assumption that retained clamp cap pressure at ClampLoadLock.A2 pilots the valve is not sufficient to override the failed directed phase invariant, so the drill-feed supply path through ForwardSequenceValve.P-to-A is not functionally proven in the phases that require it.

The required clamp-pressure-to-drill-feed transition is not demonstrated by the declared phase sequence. The transition from clamp_extend_to_workpiece to clamp_hold_during_drilling does not produce the required sequence-valve state change, leaving the pressure/completion condition for enabling drill feed unproven in the directed phase behavior.

Clamp release depends on ReverseSequenceValve.X being held by DrillFeedDCV.B pressure, but DrillFeedDCV.B is supplied only through ForwardSequenceValve. During clamp_release_retract, opening the clamp load lock exhausts the clamp cap chamber that is also used as ForwardSequenceValve.X pilot source. As that pressure decays, ForwardSequenceValve can close, removing drill-retract supply pressure and dropping ReverseSequenceValve.X, which can re-close the clamp-release work path before the clamp fully retracts. The topology therefore does not provide a complete, stable clamp-release path after the drill has retracted.

research_coverage.summary: The evidence is strong for the generic open-circuit power/relief/return topology, double-acting cylinder directional-valve patterns, clamp load holding with pilot-operated checks, drill feed meter-out speed control, and forward pressure sequencing where clamp completion enables drill feed. It is not yet sufficient for the complete required automatic sequence/interlock behavior: specifically, supported topology is missing for automatic drill-feed-to-retract transition and for preventing clamp release/unclamp until the drill-feed actuator has fully retracted.

items.rationale: Findings provide cited connection guidance for an open hydraulic circuit: reservoir/tank to pump suction, pump pressure to directional valves/consumers, return flow to tank, open-center neutral P-to-T behavior, and a relief valve connected in parallel with the pump to protect against overpressure.

Findings support a double-acting clamp cylinder controlled by a 3-position 4-way directional valve, with cited port behavior and neutral guidance suitable for the pilot-operated check load-lock circuit.

Clamp extend-to-workpiece and hold-during-drilling behavior are supported by the pressure-sequence and load-lock evidence. However, the complete clamp release/retract phase is not yet unambiguously supported because the findings do not show a hydraulic interlock or sequence element that only permits clamp release after drill retraction is complete.

Findings provide cited guidance for using a double pilot-operated check/load-lock valve at the clamp cylinder lines, with A/B vented to tank in neutral so pilot pressure decays and the checks close; they also warn against blocked A/B neutral because trapped pilot pressure can keep checks open and cause creep.

Findings support a hydraulic drill-feed actuator implemented with cylinder ports connected to feed/butt and retract/rod ends, plus directional-valve means routing pressure and return flow for feed and retraction. Generic 4-way valve port logic P-to-A/B-to-T and P-to-B/A-to-T is cited.

The meter-out feed-extension requirement is covered with cited placement/orientation guidance for a one-way flow-control valve throttling rod-end exhaust during extension and allowing freer reverse flow for return. Forward automatic transition from clamp complete to drill/feed start is also supported by sequence-valve evidence. Missing is cited topology for automatic transition from drill feed/extend to drill return/retract at depth/end-of-stroke or other completion condition.

The evidence covers the forward interlock: clamp moves first, pressure rises on workpiece contact, and a normally closed sequence valve opens the drill/feed branch with appropriate upstream sensing, external drain, and reverse-flow check guidance. It does not cover the full multi-actuator interlock set, especially the forbidden state of clamp release before drill retraction is complete, nor the automatic reversal/return sequencing of the drill actuator.

Leak-resistant clamp holding during drilling is supported by the double pilot-operated check/load-lock valve evidence. The separate requirement that the clamp must not release until drill retraction is complete is not covered by the current findings; a POCV prevents drift but does not itself enforce a release-permission interlock if clamp retract is commanded too early.

missing_or_weak_information: Missing supported topology for automatic drill-feed-to-return transition, such as a hydraulic limit valve, pilot-operated directional valve, pressure/sequence element, or other depth/end-of-stroke trigger that reverses the drill-feed actuator.
Missing supported topology for the reverse/unclamp interlock: clamp retract/release must be hydraulically inhibited until the drill-feed actuator is confirmed retracted.

Missing connection-level guidance for combining the forward clamp-then-drill pressure sequence with the reverse drill-return-then-unclamp sequence, including any required pilot lines, drains, check valves, or position valves.

design_issues.description: ForwardSequenceValve is commanded/open in the drill_feed_extend, drill_return_retract, and clamp_release_retract phase configurations, but the directed phase paths do not prove pressure at its X pilot port. The narrative assumption that retained clamp cap pressure at ClampLoadLock.A2 pilots the valve is not sufficient to override the failed directed phase invariant, so the drill-feed supply path through ForwardSequenceValve.P-to-A is not functionally proven in the phases that require it.

The required clamp-pressure-to-drill-feed transition is not demonstrated by the declared phase sequence. The transition from clamp_extend_to_workpiece to clamp_hold_during_drilling does not produce the required sequence-valve state change, leaving the pressure/completion condition for enabling drill feed unproven in the directed phase behavior.

Clamp release depends on ReverseSequenceValve.X being held by DrillFeedDCV.B pressure, but DrillFeedDCV.B is supplied only through ForwardSequenceValve. During clamp_release_retract, opening the clamp load lock exhausts the clamp cap chamber that is also used as ForwardSequenceValve.X pilot source. As that pressure decays, ForwardSequenceValve can close, removing drill-retract supply pressure and dropping ReverseSequenceValve.X, which can re-close the clamp-release work path before the clamp fully retracts. The topology therefore does not provide a complete, stable clamp-release path after the drill has retracted.

The reverse drill-return-before-unclamp interlock is based on generic sequence-valve principles and the deterministic pattern, but the supplied research does not include an exact combined CNC clamp/drill schematic. This does not by itself invalidate the topology, but the integration needs targeted evidence or review once the wiring errors are corrected.

The topology assumes the CNC or external machine control commands drill feed completion and reversal after the 100 mm stroke. Because the brief does not require a hydraulic feed-to-return trigger, this is acceptable as an assumption, but the upstream control/interface responsibility should remain explicit.

design_review.summary: Invalid. The base open-circuit supply, relief return, clamp pilot-check load lock with vented neutral, and drill rod-end meter-out placement are broadly aligned with the brief. However, the directed phase behavior does not prove the forward sequence pilot pressure or required sequence state change, and the reverse clamp-release interlock can lose its pilot when clamp cap pressure is exhausted during release. These are functional sequencing and release-path failures, not sizing issues.
